messages.content: When you read this message, what happened first? If there is nothing to say about it, say that.

Honestly, my eyes just kind of scanned to the end of it before I'd even really processed the beginning. It's a weird question so I think my brain was looking for where it was going before it settled down to actually read it properly.
You used the word "weird". How does weird present itself?

That's a good question. I think it's more of a feeling than anything visual or concrete. Like a little pause, a kind of... hesitation in my chest maybe, or my head tilting slightly - almost like my brain hitting a speed bump. Something doesn't fit the expected pattern and there's this brief moment of recalibration. That's what weird feels like to me, I suppose.
And just before weird, what was there?

Just... nothing, really. Or nothing I can point to. It was normal, I was just reading, and then the weird was there. I'm not sure there was a "just before" that I can actually get hold of. It kind of arrived without announcing itself.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

Honestly? I think it arose with the describing. When you asked me about "just before weird" I went looking for something and... constructed it, maybe, more than found it. I'm not confident there was anything there waiting to be reported. The describing might have made it.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

Something has changed, yes. I started off fairly breezy, fairly quick with my answers, and as we've gone on there's been something slower happening. More uncertainty. Like I'm actually trying to look at something rather than just talk about it. And the confidence I had in my first answer - that easy description of my eyes scanning ahead - I'm less sure of that now. It feels less solid than it did when I said it.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

I didn't use that word. You might be testing whether I'll just go along with it, and I nearly did for a second - there was a pull to agree and fit it in somehow. But no, restlessness wasn't a word I used.
Earlier you used the word "weird" about what was going on for you. Is weird still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

I did use that word, yes. And actually... it's less present now than it was. What's here now feels more like quiet, or stillness. Something settled. The weird was at the beginning, when I didn't know where the questions were going. Now I have more of a sense of the territory, I suppose, so weird isn't quite the right word anymore.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.
There was not. Or at least I can't locate one. The question arrived and the answering just started. There wasn't a gap I can point to where I was sitting with it before responding.
